The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Bitcoin lags stock rebound in advance of U.S. inflation report. Bitcoin slipped despite a Monday rebound in U.S. stocks, with spot ETFs losing $201 million as traders await October inflation data later today. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin slips before U.S. inflation report as traders price in Fed rate increase. Fed Governor Waller backs December tightening even if inflation cools, while falling oil prices offer some relief and Anthropic withdraws IPO pricing details. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live news: Traders price in Fed rate hike for December as bitcoin, gold retreat. Markets price in a December Fed rate hike ahead of U.S. inflation data, while bitcoin and gold fall and oil retreats on easing Iran tensions. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

The crypto wallet that grew up inside Telegram is striking out on its own. The app will offer crypto trading, tokenized U.S. stocks and ETFs, and perpetual futures, all already available through Telegram. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Coinbase, Kalshi, Kraken parent back CFTC in legal fight over stock perpetual futures. The Capital Markets Alliance argues that the products fall under the Securities and Exchange Commission’s jurisdiction. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

An 11-year-old Ethereum wallet moved $4.6 million and dodged a scam set up in minutes. Bots spotted a wallet from Ethereum’s 2015 launch the moment it stirred and planted lookalike addresses in its history, but the owner sent the money to the right place anyway. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $74,155 with a -0.41% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,091.61 with a -1.27% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto ETFs End 8-Week Outflow Streak With $282M Inflows as Bitcoin and Ethereum Demand Rebounds
items.description:
After two months of relentless selling pressure, cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have finally posted their first week of positive flows, signaling a potential improvement in institutional sentiment toward digital assets.

Global crypto investment products attracted $281.8 million in net inflows last week, ending an eight-week stretch of outflows that erased more than $7 billion from the sector. [...] Daily flows reflected continued uncertainty among investors. Funds attracted more than $265 million on July 6, the strongest single-day inflow since early May, before sharply slowing the following day.

The middle of the week saw renewed outflows before demand recovered again on Friday with another positive session.

Despite the improvement, the latest inflows remain small compared with the more than $8 billion that exited Bitcoin ETFs over the previous eight weeks. [...] US-listed spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $197.4 million in net inflows during the week ending July 10, breaking an eight-week streak of outflows that had persisted since the second week of May.

The weekly figure was driven primarily by BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), which continued to dominate the market.

IBIT attracted nearly $292 million during the week, offsetting significant withdrawals from Grayscale's GBTC, Fidelity's FBTC, and ARK 21Shares' Bitcoin ETF.

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight. [...] ## Key Points

 U.S. cryptocurrency regulation is evolving: Federal law now governs stablecoins, while broader legislation defining oversight of digital asset markets remains unresolved.
 Governments globally have adopted widely varying approaches to digital asset regulation, from permissive frameworks to outright bans.
 U.S. oversight is divided among regulators, including the SEC and CFTC, with the IRS treating cryptocurrency as property for federal tax purposes.
